figures.caption: Table 1. Evolution of prototype-part network modules. Inspired by Table 1 of [21].

Fig. 1. Spherical Cap Intersection Approximation. The blue spherical cap is defined by p1 as its center and its radius by the distance to zl. Similarly, the orange spherical cap is defined by p2 as its center and its radius by the distance to zl. Their intersection is approximated by the dashed red spherical with center pint, who also has its radius equal to its distance to zl. With that intersection computed, we have tighter bounds on the angular distance between an unknown prototype pk and the latent patch z.

Fig. 2. Gaussian Hypersphere Intersection Approximation. Each prototype pj is defined by its anchor µj and its variance σj (represented as a layer of the same color). In this figure, zl is at distance 2 to µ1 and distance 3 to µ2. The red dotted circle encompasses the hypersphere that approximates the intersection between the two hyperspheres in the Euclidean metric space.
